QF.id: SIA Case Studies on SAS Standards_21

question.text: Antenatal-care (ANC) check-ups are a classic SAS-200 indicator. Which of the following is the STRONGEST MoV for ANC coverage?

answer.text: Count of ANC cards distributed by the NPO
Cross-verification of PHC / ASHA registers + Mother-and-Child Protection Card (MCP card) stamps + village-level ANC camp register
A single FGD with pregnant women in one village

explanation.text: The Logic: Antenatal-care (ANC) coverage requires multi-source verification: PHC / ASHA registers (administrative data), Mother-and-Child Protection (MCP) card stamps (beneficiary-level documentary evidence), and village-level ANC camp registers (event-level evidence). Cross-verifying these independent sources is the standard triangulation approach for health-outcome indicators. The Trap: Option A counts distribution of ANC cards, not actual uptake of check-ups. Option C relies on a single FGD in a single village, which carries sample and tool bias. Option D is essentially SE self-report and lacks independent verification. Note: The specific PHC/ASHA register, MCP card stamps and village-level ANC camp register Means-of-Verification package is not enumerated in the cited Social Impact Assessors Certification Examination Workbook (January 2026) pages 123-124, 130, 133 or 174-178, which support prenatal/postnatal care and general evidence sufficiency but not this exact MoV combination. The framing above reflects general health-impact evaluation practice.
